read.sections.0.text.back: Weather is the condition of the air at one time and in one place. Weather can be hot, cold, wet, dry or windy, and it can change within a few minutes. Climate is the usual weather pattern in a place over a long period. To describe a climate, scientists usually study weather records of at least 30 years. Look at Sunrise School. The heavy rain this afternoon is weather. The fact that the rainy season has been much wetter than the dry season for 30 years is climate. Here is an easy way to remember the difference: weather is what you get today, but climate is what you expect.
read.sections.0.text.source: Weather is what the air is like at one time and place. It can be hot, cold, wet, dry or windy, and it can change in minutes. Climate is the usual pattern of weather in a place over a long time. To describe a climate, scientists usually study at least 30 years of weather records. Look at Sunrise School. Heavy rain this afternoon is weather. The fact that the rainy season has been much wetter than the dry season for 30 years is climate. Here is a simple way to remember the difference: weather is what you get today, but climate is what you expect.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: Weather is the condition of the air now. Weather can be hot or cold. Weather can be wet, dry or windy. Weather can change quickly. Climate is the usual weather in a place. It is a pattern over many years. Scientists look at records of 30 years or more. At Sunrise School, the heavy rain today is weather. The wet rainy season every year is climate. Weather is what you get today. Climate is what you expect.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: Weather is what the air is like now. It can be hot or cold. It can be wet, dry or windy. Weather can change fast. Climate is the usual weather in a place. It is a pattern over many years. Scientists look at 30 years or more. At Sunrise School, heavy rain today is weather. A wet rainy season every year is climate. Weather is what you get today. Climate is what you expect.

read.sections.1.text.back: A season is a part of the year that has its own type of weather. Far from the equator, many places have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. These seasons happen because the Earth is tilted as it moves around the Sun. Close to the equator, the weather is hot all year round, so the seasons are usually a rainy season or a dry season. In South Asia and Southeast Asia, seasonal winds called monsoons bring heavy rain for several months. In India, for example, most of the annual rain falls between June and September.
read.sections.1.text.source: A season is a part of the year with its own kind of weather. Far from the equator, many places have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. These seasons happen because Earth is tilted as it travels around the Sun. Near the equator, it is warm all year, so the seasons are usually rainy or dry instead. In South Asia and Southeast Asia, a seasonal wind called the monsoon brings heavy rain for several months. In India, for example, most of the year's rain falls between June and September.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: A season is one part of the year. Each season has its own weather. Some places have four seasons. Those seasons are spring, summer, autumn and winter. The Earth tilts a little while going around the Sun. This is what causes seasons. The equator is the line around the middle of the Earth. Places near the equator are hot all year round. There, the seasons are wet or dry. In India, a wind called the monsoon brings rain. Most of the rain falls from June to September.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: A season is a part of the year. Each season has its own weather. Some places have four seasons. They are spring, summer, autumn and winter. Earth tips a little to one side as it goes around the Sun. This makes the seasons. The equator is a line around Earth's middle. Places near it are warm all year. There, seasons are wet or dry. In India, a wind called the monsoon brings rain. Most rain falls from June to September.

read.sections.2.heading.back: People adapt themselves to climate and seasons

read.sections.2.text.note: Translator: Yemen is written as 'Yaman', the usual Malay spelling. Please confirm.
read.sections.2.text.back: People change their way of life so that it suits the climate. This change is called adaptation. In hot and dry places, such as some areas in Mali and Yemen, many buildings have thick mud-brick walls that help cool the rooms. In Mongolia, some herders move their animals between summer camps and winter camps. In many farming communities, people plant crops when the rainy season begins. Sunrise School also adapts itself. Roofed walkways make sure students do not get wet, and water stations help on hot days. Good adaptations are based on evidence and suitable for everyone, including those who use wheelchairs.
read.sections.2.text.source: People change how they live to suit their climate. These changes are called adaptations. In hot, dry places, such as parts of Mali and Yemen, many buildings have thick mud-brick walls that help keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some herders move their animals between summer and winter camps. In many farming communities, people plant crops when the rainy season begins. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered walkways keep students dry, and water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation is based on evidence and works for everyone, including people who use wheelchairs.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: People change the way they live so that it suits the climate. This is called adaptation. In some hot and dry places, houses have thick mud walls. The walls cool the rooms. In Mongolia, some families move with their animals every season. Many farmers plant seeds when the rainy season begins. Sunrise School also adapts itself. Roofed walkways make sure students do not get wet. Water stations help on hot days. Good adaptations help everyone.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: People change how they live to fit the climate. This is called adaptation. In some hot, dry places, homes have thick mud walls. The walls keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some families move with their animals each season. Many farmers plant seeds when the rains start. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered paths keep students dry. Water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation helps everyone.

watch.summary.back: This video explains how the Earth's climate is changing. Some gases in the air, such as carbon dioxide, trap heat from the Sun. These gases work a little like the glass walls of a greenhouse, which keep plants warm. People burn coal, oil and gas to get energy. This adds more of those gases to the air, so the Earth is getting hotter. The video says a hotter Earth changes weather patterns. Large areas of ice in Greenland and Antarctica are melting, and sea levels are rising. Some places now experience stronger storms and heavier rain. Other places, on the other hand, experience longer dry periods. This can make growing food difficult. The video ends with a hopeful idea. People can use energy from the sun and wind, which does not add these gases.
watch.summary.source: This video explains how Earth's climate is changing. Some gases in the air, like carbon dioxide, trap heat from the Sun. They work a bit like the glass walls of a greenhouse, which keep plants warm. People burn coal, oil and gas for energy. This adds more of these gases to the air, so Earth is getting warmer. The video says a warmer Earth changes weather patterns. Large areas of ice in Greenland and Antarctica are melting, and the sea is rising. Some places now get stronger storms and heavier rain. Other places get longer dry times. This can make it harder to grow food. The video ends with a hopeful idea. People can use power from the sun and wind, which does not add these gases.
